sentences.text: Henry Louis `` Buster '' Gehrig -LRB- born Heinrich Ludwig Gehrig ; June 19 , 1903June 2 , 1941 -RRB- was an American baseball first baseman who played 17 seasons in Major League Baseball -LRB- MLB -RRB- for the New York Yankees , from 1923 through 1939 .	New York Yankees	New York Yankees	1939	Baseball Hall of Fame balloting, 1939	baseball	baseball	first baseman	first baseman	Major League Baseball	Major League Baseball
Gehrig was renowned for his prowess as a hitter and for his durability , a trait that earned him his nickname `` The Iron Horse '' .

He was an All-Star seven consecutive times , a Triple Crown winner once , an American League -LRB- AL -RRB- Most Valuable Player twice , and a member of six World Series champion teams .	All-Star	Major League Baseball All-Star Game	World Series	World Series	Triple Crown	Major League Baseball Triple Crown	champion	List of World Series champions
He had a career .340 batting average , .632 slugging average , and a .447 on base average .	batting average	batting average	slugging average	Slugging percentage	on base average	on-base percentage
He hit 493 home runs and had 1,995 runs batted in -LRB- RBI -RRB- .	runs batted in	run batted in

In 1939 , he was elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame and was the first MLB player to have his uniform number -LRB- 4 -RRB- retired by a team .	1939	Baseball Hall of Fame balloting, 1939	Baseball Hall of Fame	Baseball Hall of Fame
A native of New York City and attendee of Columbia University , Gehrig signed with the Yankees in 1923 .	New York City	New York City	Columbia University	Columbia University

He set several major league records during his career , including the most career grand slams -LRB- 23 -RRB- -LRB- since broken by Alex Rodriguez -RRB- and most consecutive games played -LRB- 2,130 -RRB- , a record that stood for 56 years and was long considered unbreakable until surpassed by Cal Ripken , Jr. in 1995 .	grand slams	Grand slam (baseball)	Alex Rodriguez	Alex Rodriguez	most consecutive games played	Major League Baseball consecutive games played streaks	considered unbreakable	List of Major League Baseball records considered unbreakable

Gehrig 's streak ended on May 2 , 1939 , when he voluntarily took himself out of the lineup to stunned fans after his play was hampered by amyotrophic lateral sclerosis -LRB- ALS -RRB- , an incurable neuromuscular disorder now commonly referred to in North America as Lou Gehrig 's disease .	1939	Baseball Hall of Fame balloting, 1939	amyotrophic lateral sclerosis	amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
The disease forced him to retire at age 36 and was the cause of his death two years later .

The pathos of his farewell from baseball was capped off by his iconic 1939 `` Luckiest Man on the Face of the Earth '' speech at Yankee Stadium .	1939	Baseball Hall of Fame balloting, 1939	baseball	baseball	Yankee Stadium	Yankee Stadium

Gehrig was voted the greatest first baseman of all time by the Baseball Writers ' Association in 1969 , and was the leading vote-getter on the Major League Baseball All-Century Team chosen by fans in 1999 .
